overall_summary: Bitcoin faces mixed forces with heavy ETF outflows and a stronger dollar from firm hike odds weighed against large off-exchange accumulation, Strategy buying, and a supportive CFTC reserves ruling. Geopolitical headlines stay noisy while markets wait on core PCE and GDP. The near-term tone for crypto is balanced and data-dependent.
key_points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs see large weekly outflows
Institutions scoop nearly $1B BTC off exchanges
CFTC lets BTC and ether count as reserves
Dollar strength and hike bets pressure risk
Markets brace for core PCE and GDP

items.title: BTC Rebounds From $55K Low on Nvidia CEO Return, Short Squeeze
items.summary: Bitcoin swung from a two-year low near fifty-five thousand over the weekend to as high as sixty-four thousand five hundred on Monday after Nvidia reinstated founder Jensen Huang as CEO, sending the stock up more than thirty percent and lifting risk assets. Hundreds of millions in short positions were liquidated in the squeeze, including roughly two hundred fifty million in a ten-minute window. The move later faded with price slipping back toward sixty-one to sixty-two thousand as US-hours selling returned. Traders should care because the bounce was leverage-driven and tied to tech sentiment; it needs fresh spot demand to hold.
items.impact: Short-term relief rally that may fade without ETF inflows

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.8B Weekly, $669M Friday Outflow
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about one point seven nine billion dollars in net outflows for the week of November sixteen to twenty, with six hundred sixty-nine million leaving on Friday alone, the largest single day since June. BlackRock IBIT led the redemptions. November outflows are already multi-billion and analysts call the selling structural amid rate-hike fears. This matters because ETF flows have been a primary price driver; continued redemptions cap rebounds and signal institutional caution heading into PCE data.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure that limits upside until flows turn

items.title: Abraxas Capital Scoops Roughly $1B Bitcoin Off Exchanges
items.summary: On-chain trackers including Lookonchain and Arkham flagged wallets linked to Abraxas Capital withdrawing approximately seventeen thousand five hundred ninety-seven BTC, worth about one point zero four billion dollars, from Binance and Kraken over two days during the sub-sixty thousand dip. Average entry was near fifty-nine thousand two hundred. The firm later added more, pushing linked holdings higher. Traders should watch this because large cold-wallet accumulation during panic removes supply from exchanges and often marks institutional dip-buying.
items.impact: Supply absorption that supports a local floor if sustained

items.title: CFTC Lets BTC, Ether, Stablecoins Count Toward Reserves
items.summary: CFTC staff issued an advisory allowing bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins to count toward the twelve-month operating-cost financial resources that derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses must hold, subject to haircuts of at least twenty percent for BTC and ETH and two percent for stablecoins. Crypto still cannot meet the separate liquidity requirement. This is staff guidance only, not a Commission rule. It gives regulated crypto venues more balance-sheet flexibility and is a constructive regulatory signal.
items.impact: Positive clarity that eases capital burdens for crypto derivatives firms

items.title: Strategy Buys 457 BTC, Lifts Preferred Buyback Cap to $4B
items.summary: Michael Saylor’s Strategy added four hundred fifty-seven bitcoin for twenty-nine point six million dollars last week at an average near sixty-four thousand nine hundred, bringing holdings to eight hundred fifty-one thousand three hundred five BTC. The firm spent far more, two hundred twelve million, buying back its STRC preferred stock and raised that repurchase authorization to four billion dollars while moving one billion from its USD reserve into flexible cash. Accumulation continues but has slowed versus preferred buybacks. It remains a steady institutional bid even as the stock and bitcoin have been under pressure.
items.impact: Steady treasury demand that cushions downside but size is modest vs ETF flows

items.title: Grayscale Calls Bitcoin Oversold; AI Risks Cloud Near Term
items.summary: Grayscale research said bitcoin’s drop to about fifty-five thousand extended the current bear market to at least four hundred eleven days, the longest in its comparison, yet the fifty-six percent drawdown from the October twenty twenty-five peak is the shallowest. The firm sees major cryptos as oversold after heavy ETP outflows, stablecoin redemptions and put demand, with solid blockchain fundamentals offering a longer-term entry. Near-term prices, however, hinge more on AI-related volatility than on-chain metrics. This frames the washout as potentially constructive while warning that tech headlines still dominate.
items.impact: Supports longer-term accumulation view but leaves near-term direction unresolved

items.title: Fed's Williams: Still Work to Do on High Inflation
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that inflation remains too high at around three and a half percent and the central bank still has work to do to bring it back to the two percent target on a sustained basis. He pointed to resilient growth, a stable labor market, and the need for actions over time, with markets fully pricing a quarter-point hike at the December meeting. Crypto traders should care because this locks in higher-for-longer rates expectations right before key PCE data, keeping pressure on risk assets.
items.impact: Supports higher rates, stronger dollar, and tighter financial conditions weighing on Bitcoin

items.title: US Flash PMIs Cool but Still Signal Solid Growth
items.summary: S and P Global flash PMIs for November showed the composite easing to fifty four point six, services dropping to fifty four point seven below forecasts, and manufacturing holding at fifty four point five. Growth slowed due to high prices and capacity constraints but remains expansionary and still points to about three percent annualized fourth-quarter GDP. Traders watch this as an early read on demand strength heading into PCE and the Fed decision, with hiring still solid.
items.impact: Cooling momentum but resilient activity leaves December hike odds intact

items.title: Dollar Hits Near 19-Month Highs on Hike Bets
items.summary: The US dollar index climbed to around one hundred four point three, its strongest levels in about nineteen months, lifted by firming December rate-hike expectations and recovering risk appetite after the Nvidia-led rebound. Ten-year yields hovered near four point nine two to four point nine five percent while the two-year rose on policy bets. A strong dollar typically pressures crypto and commodities, so this remains a key headwind for Bitcoin traders.
items.impact: Stronger DXY and rate differentials squeeze risk assets including crypto

items.title: Markets Brace for Core PCE and GDP Wednesday
items.summary: The key inflation gauge Core PCE for October and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP both drop Wednesday at eight thirty Eastern, alongside personal income, durable goods, and jobless claims. Consensus looks for Core PCE around zero point three percent month-over-month and GDP holding near three point four percent. This is the last major data before the December FOMC and will heavily influence whether hike odds stay near one hundred percent or ease.
items.impact: High-stakes catalyst that could lock in or soften December rate-hike pricing

items.title: Consumer Confidence and Industrial Data Due Today
items.summary: Tuesday's calendar features Conference Board Consumer Confidence for November expected near ninety two from ninety one point seven, plus Case-Shiller home prices and Industrial Production with the annual revision. These give fresh reads on household sentiment and factory activity just ahead of the bigger PCE release. Soft or strong prints can nudge yields and the dollar intraday, affecting crypto volatility into the holiday-shortened week.
items.impact: Secondary data that may fine-tune rate expectations before PCE

items.title: Treasury Yields Steady as Hike Odds Firm Near 96-100%
items.summary: The ten-year yield closed near four point nine two to four point nine five percent while shorter yields rose with markets pricing a near-certain twenty-five basis point December hike and elevated odds of further tightening. Williams' remarks and the stock rebound reduced safe-haven buying. Higher real yields and a firm dollar remain a structural drag on Bitcoin until inflation data clearly cools.
items.impact: Elevated yields reinforce higher-for-longer regime pressuring risk assets

items.title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship in Libya with sea drones
items.summary: President Zelenskyy confirmed Ukraine used seven naval drones to sink Russia's relatively new corvette Merkury at Benghazi port and hit a cargo ship allegedly carrying weapons. This is a major expansion of the war far beyond the Black Sea into the Mediterranean. Traders should watch for Russian retaliation threats and higher shipping insurance costs that could spill into broader risk sentiment.
items.impact: Raises escalation risk and war-risk premiums on risk assets

items.title: Iran vows all means to break US naval blockade
items.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said it will use every tool available to confront the US naval blockade of its ports, calling it military aggression and citing self-defense rights. Reports suggest tankers may attempt to challenge the blockade while Hormuz traffic remains disrupted and uncertain. This keeps oil markets jumpy and elevates the chance of a sharp energy shock that hits risk assets.
items.impact: Heightens oil volatility and geopolitical risk premium

items.title: COP31 climate summit collapses with no fossil fuel deal
items.summary: The longest UN climate talks on record in Turkey ended without a main political agreement after the EU, UK and others rejected a text that omitted any mention of fossil fuels. Deep splits over energy security amid ongoing wars and high prices killed consensus. For markets this reinforces that oil and gas will stay central longer, supporting energy prices but offering little new policy clarity.
items.impact: Supports longer-term fossil fuel demand narrative

items.title: EU unveils 22nd Russia sanctions package on banks and fleet
items.summary: European Commission President von der Leyen proposed a new sanctions round targeting around 60 more Russian banks for SWIFT removal, crypto platforms, over 70 shadow fleet vessels, refinery repair bans, ex-soldiers' visas and Russian athletes. It aims to further squeeze Moscow's war financing. This adds incremental pressure on Russia but is unlikely to shift the battlefield overnight.
items.impact: Mild additional pressure on Russian economy and energy flows

items.title: Libya reopens key oil pipeline, easing supply fears
items.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation said the pipeline from the giant Sharara field reopened after a brief closure by an armed group that had threatened about 350,000 barrels per day of output. Brent briefly dipped below 90 dollars on the news amid other supply signals. Extra Libyan barrels provide a near-term cushion against Middle East disruptions and support risk appetite if oil cools further.
items.impact: Temporary oil price relief that can lift risk assets

items.title: China threatens countermeasures over US telecom ban
items.summary: China's commerce ministry firmly opposed the FCC vote barring major Chinese telecom firms from direct access to US phone numbers and warned of necessary countermeasures. The move continues tech decoupling and follows earlier lab-testing restrictions. Fresh US-China friction risks weighing on global growth expectations and tech-related risk assets if retaliation expands.
items.impact: Adds to US-China tech and trade uncertainty
